checks.title: Keep privileged user accounts cloud-native
checks.description: Privileged Entra role holders should not depend on an on-premises identity source.
checks.rationale: A separate cloud authentication boundary reduces exposure to an on-premises compromise.
checks.business_impact: Synced privileged identities can extend an Active Directory compromise into Microsoft 365.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Migrate active privileged role holders to dedicated cloud-only accounts.
checks.remediation: Create dedicated cloud-only administrator identities, transfer role assignments, and protect them with strong Conditional Access.

checks.title: Maintain a resilient number of Global Administrators
checks.description: The tenant should have between two and four active Global Administrator users.
checks.rationale: Too few administrators harms recovery, while too many increases the privileged attack surface.
checks.business_impact: Poorly balanced Global Administrator coverage can cause lockout or excessive privilege exposure.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Review direct and role-assignable-group Global Administrator membership.
checks.remediation: Retain two to four dedicated Global Administrators and use lower-privileged roles for routine work.

checks.title: Prevent ordinary users from registering applications
checks.description: Default users should not be permitted to create application registrations.
checks.rationale: Controlled application onboarding reduces unreviewed identities and delegated access paths.
checks.business_impact: Unrestricted registrations can introduce shadow applications and consent risk.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Set allowedToCreateApps to false in the authorization policy.
checks.remediation: Disable application registration for default users and delegate application creation through an approved role or process.

checks.title: Prevent ordinary users from creating tenants
checks.description: Non-administrators should not be able to create new Entra tenants from the organization.
checks.rationale: Tenant creation should be governed to avoid unmanaged organizational directories.
checks.business_impact: Unmanaged tenants can become shadow-IT environments outside security oversight.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Set allowedToCreateTenants to false for the default user role.
checks.remediation: Restrict tenant creation to approved administrators through the Entra authorization policy.

checks.title: Restrict security-group creation to administrators
checks.description: Default users should not be allowed to create security groups.
checks.rationale: Security groups are authorization primitives and should follow a governed creation process.
checks.business_impact: Uncontrolled group creation can lead to inconsistent access assignments and privilege sprawl.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Set allowedToCreateSecurityGroups to false.
checks.remediation: Disable security-group creation in default user role permissions and provide a managed request path.

checks.title: Govern Microsoft 365 group creation
checks.description: General users should not be able to create Microsoft 365 groups without an approved scope.
checks.rationale: A controlled group lifecycle reduces abandoned workspaces and unmanaged collaboration surfaces.
checks.business_impact: Unrestricted creation increases data sprawl, ownership gaps, and external-sharing exposure.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Limit group creation through the Group.Unified tenant setting.
checks.remediation: Configure Group.Unified with EnableGroupCreation false and, if needed, specify an approved creator group.

checks.title: Limit who can join devices to Entra ID
checks.description: Device join should be denied by default or scoped to selected identities.
checks.rationale: Restricting device join reduces attacker persistence through unauthorized device identities.
checks.business_impact: Broad device join rights can allow unmanaged devices to appear trusted.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value did not satisfy the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Replace the all-users join scope with selected identities or no user scope.
checks.remediation: Scope Entra join to a managed group or disable user-driven joining where it is unnecessary.

checks.title: Cap user device registrations at ten
checks.description: A user should be limited to no more than ten Entra joined or registered devices.
checks.rationale: A bounded quota constrains unauthorized enrollment and reduces stale device identities.
checks.business_impact: Excessive quotas can support persistence and complicate device governance.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Configure a device quota of ten or fewer.
checks.remediation: Set userDeviceQuota to ten or fewer; use Device Enrollment Manager accounts for approved bulk enrollment.

checks.title: Do not make Global Administrators local device administrators automatically
checks.description: Global Administrator membership should not automatically grant local administrator rights during Entra join.
checks.rationale: Separating cloud administration from endpoint administration limits privilege concentration.
checks.business_impact: Automatic local rights increase credential exposure and lateral-movement impact.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Use dedicated endpoint administration roles instead of Global Administrators.
checks.remediation: Disable enableGlobalAdmins in the Entra join local administrator policy.

checks.title: Limit local administrators assigned during device join
checks.description: Registering users should not universally receive local administrator rights on joined devices.
checks.rationale: Selected administrative groups provide tighter endpoint privilege control than all registering users.
checks.business_impact: Broad local administration increases malware execution and credential theft risk.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Use an enumerated or empty registering-users scope.
checks.remediation: Scope registering-user local administration to selected users/groups or disable it.

checks.title: Enable Entra Local Administrator Password Solution
checks.description: The tenant device registration policy should enable Local Administrator Password Solution.
checks.rationale: Unique, rotated local administrator passwords reduce credential reuse across endpoints.
checks.business_impact: Shared or unmanaged local passwords enable lateral movement after endpoint compromise.
checks.observation: Mock permission gap prevented collection of the required evidence.
checks.recommendation: Set localAdminPassword.isEnabled to true.
checks.remediation: Enable Microsoft Entra LAPS and deploy the corresponding device policy to supported endpoints.

checks.title: Restrict users from reading their stored BitLocker keys
checks.description: Default users should not be able to retrieve BitLocker recovery keys for owned devices.
checks.rationale: Recovery-key access should follow a controlled support and authorization process.
checks.business_impact: Compromised user accounts could expose recovery material for organizational devices.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Provide key recovery through approved support roles and workflows.
checks.remediation: Disable allowedToReadBitlockerKeysForOwnedDevice in default user role permissions.

checks.title: Block default end-user application consent
checks.description: Default user role permissions should not assign self-service permission-grant policies.
checks.rationale: Central consent review reduces malicious or excessive delegated application access.
checks.business_impact: Unreviewed consent can expose mail, files, profiles, and other organizational data.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Keep permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned empty for default users.
checks.remediation: Remove permission grant policies from the default user role and use the admin consent workflow.

checks.title: Enable the application admin consent request workflow
checks.description: Users should have a governed method to request administrator review for application consent.
checks.rationale: A review workflow supports business access without restoring unmanaged user consent.
checks.business_impact: Without a workflow, users may seek unapproved workarounds or requests may be inconsistently reviewed.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value did not satisfy the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Set the admin consent request policy isEnabled property to true.
checks.remediation: Enable the admin consent request policy and assign qualified reviewers with notifications.

checks.title: Block new application password credentials
checks.description: The tenant application management policy should block password and symmetric-key additions for applications and service principals.
checks.rationale: Certificates and workload federation provide stronger proof-of-possession than reusable client secrets.
checks.business_impact: Leaked client secrets can permit direct authentication as highly privileged workloads.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Migrate workloads to certificates or federated identity before enforcing the restriction.
checks.remediation: Enable tenant-wide passwordAddition and symmetricKeyAddition restrictions for applications and service principals.

checks.title: Limit application password credentials to 180 days
checks.description: New application and service-principal password credentials should have a maximum lifetime of 180 days.
checks.rationale: Shorter credential lifetimes reduce the useful window for a stolen secret.
checks.business_impact: Long-lived secrets can remain exploitable long after an unnoticed disclosure.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Automate rotation and move toward secretless workload identity.
checks.remediation: Enable passwordLifetime and symmetricKeyLifetime restrictions with P180D or shorter values.

checks.title: Require system-generated application passwords
checks.description: Custom caller-supplied password credentials should be blocked for applications and service principals.
checks.rationale: System-generated values avoid predictable, low-entropy, or reused workload passwords.
checks.business_impact: Weak custom credentials are easier to guess, reuse, or expose in automation.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Update automation to accept system-generated secret values.
checks.remediation: Enable customPasswordAddition restrictions for applications and service principals.

checks.title: Limit application certificates to 180 days
checks.description: New application and service-principal certificates should have a maximum lifetime of 180 days.
checks.rationale: Regular certificate rotation limits the lifetime of compromised private keys.
checks.business_impact: Long-lived certificates extend the period in which stolen workload identity material remains valid.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Automate certificate issuance and rotation before enforcement.
checks.remediation: Enable asymmetricKeyLifetime restrictions with P180D or shorter values for applications and service principals.

checks.title: Keep guest directory visibility limited
checks.description: Guests should receive the limited or restricted guest directory role, not member-equivalent visibility.
checks.rationale: Limited directory visibility reduces reconnaissance available to compromised guest identities.
checks.business_impact: Member-equivalent guest access can expose users, groups, and membership relationships.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Use one of the two restricted guest role templates.
checks.remediation: Select limited guest access or the most restrictive guest access option in External Identities settings.

checks.title: Limit who can invite guest users
checks.description: Guest invitations should be limited to designated administrative roles or disabled.
checks.rationale: A governed invitation path reduces unauthorized external identities in the tenant.
checks.business_impact: Broad invitation rights can create unmanaged guest access and data-sharing paths.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Assign Guest Inviter only through an approved workflow.
checks.remediation: Set allowInvitesFrom to adminsAndGuestInviters or none and document the invitation process.

checks.title: Make every active member user MFA-capable
checks.description: Every member represented by the registration report should be capable of completing MFA.
checks.rationale: MFA capability is a prerequisite for resilient access policies and account recovery.
checks.business_impact: Users without registered strong authentication remain more exposed to credential theft.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value did not satisfy the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Track registration coverage until no active member is reported as not MFA capable.
checks.remediation: Run an authentication-method registration campaign and resolve every member lacking MFA capability.

checks.title: Disable SMS and voice authentication methods
checks.description: SMS and voice call authentication should be disabled as tenant authentication methods.
checks.rationale: Telephony methods are susceptible to interception, redirection, and social-engineering attacks.
checks.business_impact: Weak authentication methods can undermine otherwise strong access policy requirements.
checks.observation: Mock permission gap prevented collection of the required evidence.
checks.recommendation: Prefer phishing-resistant credentials and Microsoft Authenticator where appropriate.
checks.remediation: Disable SMS and voice authentication methods after migrating users to stronger methods.

checks.title: Disable email one-time passcodes as an authentication method
checks.description: The tenant authentication-method policy should disable email OTP.
checks.rationale: Email OTP inherits the security of an external mailbox and is weaker than managed strong authentication.
checks.business_impact: Compromise of an external mailbox can enable authentication to tenant resources.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Use managed federation or stronger authentication for external identities.
checks.remediation: Disable the email authentication method after validating external identity sign-in requirements.

checks.title: Require number matching for Microsoft Authenticator users
checks.description: Microsoft Authenticator should be enabled and number matching should target all users.
checks.rationale: Number matching reduces accidental approval and common MFA push-fatigue attacks.
checks.business_impact: Simple approve/deny prompts can be abused through repeated attacker-generated requests.
checks.observation: The synthetic tenant value satisfied the expected condition.
checks.recommendation: Combine number matching with application and location context.
checks.remediation: Enable Microsoft Authenticator number matching for the all_users target and review exclusions.

findings.rationale: Tenant-wide collaboration and meeting controls reduce exposure to untrusted users, content, and applications.
findings.business_impact: Permissive Teams policies can create unauthorized communication, file-sharing, recording, and meeting access paths.
findings.observation: The synthetic tenant value did not satisfy the expected condition.
findings.recommendation: Review effective policy assignments and test changes with representative collaboration scenarios.
findings.remediation: Disable PSTN lobby bypass in each effective meeting policy.
